plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Alveolar Diffusion, Haemoglobin Cooperativity & Pulmonary Surfactant chart from Hooke & Lower (October 1667 / 1669 Tractatus de Corde), Christian Bohr, Hasselbalch & Krogh (1904 Skand. Arch. Physiol. 16: 402–412), August & Marie Krogh (1910 Skand. Arch. Physiol. 23: 179–278), Neergaard (1929 Z. Gesamte Exp. Med. 66: 373–394), Avery & Mead (May 1959 AMA J. Dis. Child. 97: 517–523), and Perutz et al. (13 February 1960 Nature 185: 416–422) shows alveolar oxygen tension always exceeding arterial blood PO2 (~100 vs ~95 mmHg, passive diffusion across 300 million alveoli / ~70–100 m2), the sigmoidal O2 dissociation curve (T-to-R cooperative shift + right-shift Bohr Effect), and DPPC surfactant slashing alveolar surface tension from ~50 to <5 dyn/cm.

teach_overlay.label: 300M ALVEOLI (70–100 M2), KROGH PASSIVE DIFFUSION, BOHR/PERUTZ HAEMOGLOBIN S-CURVE & AVERY SURFACTANT (<5 DYN/CM)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked alveolar gas-exchange, haemoglobin S-curve & surfactant surface-tension chart on period paper showing 300,000,000 alveoli (~70–100 m2 area, 0.5 µm barrier), Krogh's passive diffusion gradient (alveolar PO2 > capillary PO2), Bohr & Perutz's 4-subunit haemoglobin cooperative O2 curve, and Avery's pulmonary surfactant lowering surface tension from ~50 dyn/cm to near 0 dyn/cm on exhalation
teach_overlay.scale: your two lungs fold the surface area of an entire singles tennis court inside your ribcage — and every red blood cell races across that court in three-quarters of a second, snapping up oxygen through a wall fifty times thinner than tissue paper
